name: qd
why: Double-double and quad-double arithmetic from David Bailey, real numerical math with extended precision for pi-style computation.

brief.what_it_is: QD is a double-double and quad-double extended-precision arithmetic package for C++ and Fortran-90, written by David H. Bailey with Xiaoye Li and Yozo Hida at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. The homepage describes double-double as about 31 digits and quad-double as about 62 digits. A program that uses its high-level interface swaps in these higher-precision number types for ordinary floating-point values. Results come out with many more correct digits than standard double precision. The homepage lists QD as an older package, and the detail section confirms it is a library rather than a standalone tool.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit motivation for QD. It sits in a directory of Bailey's high-precision software, and the entry frames it as older, with new users pointed to DQFUN, QXFUN or DDFUN instead.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internals. It says only that the package provides double-double and quad-double functionality through a Fortran-90 and a C++ high-level interface. The mechanism is not described there.
brief.install_notes: The homepage links to a GitHub page for QD, but the page text gives no URL, so I did not follow it. The text says QD runs on Unix-based systems, including Apple OS X. If Safari unzips the download automatically, rename the file (example given: qd-2.3.24.tar.gz to qd-2.3.24.tar) before extracting. Commercial use requires contacting the Intellectual Property Office at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (ipo@lbl.gov). The license is the LBNL-BSD modified BSD license, in LBNL-BSD-License.txt or .docx on the homepage. No build commands or configuration steps appear on this page.
brief.standout: QD is one of the few packages that offers two precision tiers, double-double and quad-double, behind both Fortran-90 and C++ interfaces. The homepage positions it as the older member of a family whose newer members (DDFUN, QXFUN, DQFUN) target the same extended-precision niche with Fortran-2008 compilers.
brief.status: Quiet. The homepage labels QD as "An older quad-double package" and tells new users to use DQFUN, QXFUN or DDFUN. The directory page itself shows "Updated: 16 October 2026", but that date covers the directory, not QD, and I found no QD release date or commit date on the page.
brief.caveats: QD is not thread-safe, according to the homepage. The page does not say whether it is still being developed. The homepage gives QD's precision as about 60 digits in the list and about 62 digits in the detail section, so the figures are inconsistent. The brew scout note says QD is for "pi-style computation", but the homepage does not say that. The scout note is unverified. The license has a commercial-use restriction that requires contacting the lab. The homepage was reachable; the GitHub README was not followed because no URL was given.
quotes: QD: An older quad-double package (approx. 60 digits) for Fortran and C++ (new users should use DQFUN, QXFUN or DDFUN).
This package is an older package that provides double-double (approximately 31-digit precision) and quad-double (approximately 62-digit precision) functionality.
It is not thread-safe, but, unlike MPFUN2020, is available with both a Fortran-90 and a C++ high-level interface.
fetch_log: https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbsoftware/ — fetched OK; directory page covering MPFUN2020, DQFUN, QXFUN, DDFUN, MPFUN2015, ARPREC and QD. QD section has no direct download URL; it points to an unlinked GitHub page.
